tasks.gr12-listening-speaking-t1: Topic: Prepared speech, listening comprehension, discussion, oral response, register control. Grade 12 FAL learners revise speech structure (intshayelelo, umzimba, isiphetho), refine listening strategies (predicting, noting key words, inferring), engage in critical discussions with register awareness, and respond analytically to literary texts using P-E-E structure. Ask learners to identify speech structural elements, choose correct listening strategies, demonstrate discussion etiquette, cite evidence in oral responses, and distinguish formal from informal register.
tasks.gr12-reading-viewing-t1: Topic: Prescribed literature, visual literacy, comprehension, summary, critical reading. Grade 12 FAL learners read literary and non-literary texts analytically, practise summary writing of 3-5 points, analyse visual texts (cartoons, advertisements, photographs), interpret themes and character development, and answer Paper 1 and Paper 2 style comprehension questions. Ask learners to identify main ideas, write concise summaries, interpret visual features, analyse character motivation with evidence, and distinguish fact from opinion.
tasks.gr12-writing-presenting-t1: Topic: Essay planning, reflective or narrative writing, transactional texts, drafting and editing. Grade 12 FAL learners produce exam-ready essays with clear thesis statements, paragraph development using TEEL (Topic, Explain, Evidence, Link), and varied sentence structures. They also write transactional texts (formal letters, reports) with correct format and tone. Ask learners to identify essay structure elements, choose effective planning strategies, apply TEEL paragraph structure, recognise correct transactional format features, and identify editing improvements.
tasks.gr12-language-structures-t1: Topic: Advanced editing, isiXhosa concord (isivumelwano), punctuation, style, vocabulary in context. Grade 12 FAL learners refine accuracy by applying isiXhosa noun-class concord rules, correcting punctuation in complex sentences, inferring vocabulary meaning from context, and improving style through word choice and sentence variety. Ask learners to apply concord rules correctly, identify and correct punctuation errors, infer word meaning from context, choose more effective vocabulary, and identify style improvements.
